title: An HTML comment inside an inline `<span>` splits the paragraph in two
spec:
This is the Python-Markdown library (Python 3, no dependencies). Run the tests with `python3 run_tests.py`. When an HTML comment sits on its own line inside an inline element that is closed in the same paragraph, the comment is pulled out as a block and the paragraph is split around it, leaving broken, unbalanced HTML. Input: `markdown.markdown(' ')` Expected: `

` Actual: `

` The same happens when the closing tag follows the comment on the same line (` ` should give `

`). A comment that is on the same line as the opening tag already works. A comment should only be split out when the inline element is not closed in that paragraph: if the comment is separated by blank lines, the element is left unclosed, or the comment follows already-closed or void inline HTML, the current block-level handling should stay.
acceptance: The reported inputs keep the comment inside the paragraph
Comments after blank lines, after an unclosed inline tag, or after closed or void inline HTML are still output as separate blocks as today
